A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across formatting changes and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments on Dolly and ELI5, including accuracy, pAUC, computational savings, entropy analyses and attack evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds calibration-resampling results and an analysis of learned logistic-regression decision boundaries.

M1.justification: The watermarking methods, detector features, one- and two-sided cascades, logistic regression, MLP and decision tree remain unchanged. The new decision-boundary analysis examines the existing logistic-regression model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Dolly and ELI5 tasks, C4 reference samples, human and other-model negatives, and paraphrasing and token-replacement scenarios. The added analyses reuse the existing Gemma/Dolly/Aaronson setting.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same watermark schemes and LLh, DetectLLM/LLR, RoBERTa, Binoculars and RADAR detectors. The model-negative comparisons retain their existing LLh, LLR and RoBERTa subset. Newly cited attack methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds an evaluation design that holds test samples fixed while resampling calibration data and refitting models and decision thresholds. Existing dataset splits, model configurations, decoding settings, metrics and attack procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds calibration-sensitivity testing in Table 2 and examines the relative use of watermark and non-watermark scores through learned decision boundaries in Figure 4. Existing entropy, text-length and corruption analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 describes classwise test-set bootstrapping without specifying its count; v2 specifies 500 resamples while retaining the two-standard-error convention. V2 also reports accuracy standard deviations from 100 calibration resamples with refitting. The disclosure does not establish an increase in resampling for existing results.

E6.justification: All 22 original tables and five original figures retain their results after matching renumbered content. New Table 2 reports calibration-induced variability, including standard deviations of 0.051 for RoBERTa-based LR versus 0.649 and 0.647 for the two cascades. Figure 4 adds learned decision-boundary results.

T1.justification: The entropy identities, watermark-score definitions, detector formulas and Appendix A.1 discussion of multiple-threshold ROC evaluation are retained. The added empirical analyses introduce no substantive formal definitions, assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about complementary detection signals, low-entropy benefits and the recommendations for cascades and logistic regression. The introduction's added 75%-to-over-95% example illustrates the existing low-entropy claim using previously plotted evidence.

C2.justification: V2 explains why prompt-matched negatives make detection harder, acknowledges more advanced attacks, and interprets calibration stability and learned score weighting. However, Figure 4's claim that non-watermark weighting is more pronounced for RoBERTa conflicts with its comparatively steeper plotted boundary.

D1.justification: The implementation, classifier hyperparameters, software version, hardware, compute budget, preprocessing instructions and model/data/code links are retained. The additional resampling information concerns statistical estimation and evaluation design.

R1.justification: V2 adds Cheng et al. (2025) on watermark rewrite attacks and Lu et al. (2023) and Kumarage et al. (2023) on evasive prompting. It expands the discussion of detection evasion using the retained Krishna/DIPPER citation, while preserving the central positioning relative to earlier hybrid detection work.

P1.justification: Localized additions explain the motivating performance example, attack selection, negative-sample difficulty and new appendix analyses. Section 3.6 changes from 'Adversarial Attacks' to 'Attacks', and publication information is updated. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds decision-boundary Figure 4 and calibration-variability Table 2, renumbering subsequent appendix displays. The TMLR template changes typography, headers, margins and placement, while retaining existing plot graphics and table structures.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves empirical transparency through calibration-stability evidence absent from v1 and an explicit test-bootstrap count. These gains concern a limited setting and leave the main benchmark findings unchanged. The benefit is partly offset by Figure 4's incorrect y >= x decision-region description and its RoBERTa-weight interpretation, which conflicts with the plotted slopes.
